body.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\), the projection of \(\Theta(P)\) onto \((p_{11},\ldots,p_{LL})\) is exactly \(\prod_{d=1}^{L}[\ell_d,u_d]\). Every vector in this box admits an upper-triangular nonnegative completion with row margins \(r\) and column margins \(c\), including when observable cells are zero.
body.justification: The box projection is the structural cancellation that removes the high-dimensional response-type optimizer.
body.gap: Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Theorem 1(iii) already gives sharp closed-form weighted aggregate LCDE bounds, but it does not state the simultaneous Cartesian projection of all positive-layer diagonal response-type masses.
body.consumer: Software for protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiments can replace response-table enumeration by \(2L\) observable diagonal endpoints.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\).  By the definitions of \(\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\) and \(\mathcal V_{L,\kappa}\),
\[
C_d\le R_d\quad(d=0,\ldots,L-1),
\]
and \(C_L=R_L=1\).  First consider any \(p\in\Theta(P)\).  Upper triangularity implies
\[
p_{dd}\le r_d,\qquad p_{dd}\le c_d.
\]
Moreover, all mass in columns \(0,\ldots,d\), except for \(p_{dd}\), comes from rows \(0,\ldots,d-1\).  Consequently
\[
C_d\le R_{d-1}+p_{dd},
\]
so
\[
\ell_d=\max\{0,C_d-R_{d-1}\}\le p_{dd}le \min\{r_d,c_d\}=u_d.
\]
This proves that the diagonal projection is contained in the asserted box.

For the converse, fix arbitrary numbers \(x_d\in[\ell_d,u_d]\), \(d=1,\ldots,L\).  The compatibility inequalities imply that these intervals are nonempty: indeed,
\[
C_d-R_{d-1}\le r_d
\]
by \(C_d\le R_d=R_{d-1}+r_d\), and
\[
C_d-R_{d-1}=c_d+C_{d-1}-R_{d-1}\le c_d.
\]
Set \(p_{00}=c_0\), \(p_{dd}=x_d\) for \(d\ge1\), and define the residual row and column masses
\[
\alpha_0=r_0-c_0,qquad \alpha_i=r_i-x_i\ (i=1,\ldots,L),qquad
\beta_j=c_j-x_j\ (j=1,\ldots,L).
\]
They are nonnegative.  Also \(x_L=r_L\): since \(C_L=R_L=1\),
\[
\ell_L=C_L-R_{L-1}=r_L,
\]
whereas \(u_L\le r_L\).  Hence \(\alpha_L=0\).  The residual totals agree,
\[
\sum_{i=0}^{L-1}\alpha_i=1-c_0-\sum_{d=1}^Lx_d
=\sum_{j=1}^L\beta_j,
\]
and, for every \(d=1,\ldots,L\),
\[
\sum_{j=1}^d\beta_j
=C_d-c_0-\sum_{j=1}^d x_j
\le R_{d-1}-c_0-\sum_{i=1}^{d-1}x_i
=\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}\alpha_i,
\]
where the inequality is exactly \(x_d\ge C_d-R_{d-1}\).

These inequalities give a constructive strict-triangular completion.  Process columns \(j=1,\ldots,L\) in increasing order.  Before filling column \(j\), earlier columns have consumed exactly \(\sum_{k=1}^{j-1}\beta_k\) from rows \(0,\ldots,j-2\).  Thus the total unconsumed mass in eligible rows \(0,\ldots,j-1\) is
\[
\sum_{i=0}^{j-1}\alpha_i-\sum_{k=1}^{j-1}\beta_k\ge\beta_j.
\]
Take mass successively from those rows until demand \(\beta_j\) is met, and denote the resulting allocations by \(p_{ij}\) for \(i<j\).  Nonnegativity is preserved at every step.  After column \(L\), equality of the residual totals shows that all residual row mass has been exhausted.  Together with the fixed diagonal, this gives a nonnegative upper-triangular array having row margins \(r\), column margins \(c\), and \(p_{dd}=x_d\).  The construction uses only weak inequalities and nonnegative residual masses, so zero observable cells cause no exception.  Thus the projection is exactly \(\prod_{d=1}^L[\ell_d,u_d]\).
